analysis:
This PR changes documentation only; no Swift source was supplied.

inference.md: the single change, head line 2371, adds a failure-mode row. Autopilot placement holds exclude a slot from eviction and give its weights no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit. This is availability behavior that fails closed: loads are refused, not overcommitted. The rest of units 14 and 15 is unchanged context covering MiMo, Flint, Qwen4 and Bonsai. I found no regression in it relative to T-041, T-008 or TB-007.

model-autopilot.md (head lines 3-265) documents several new behaviors:
- The Autopilot set equals the persisted selection plus all verified cached catalog builds, capped at 256.
- Downloads are on by default with saved consent. They run through the ordinary manifest-verified prefetch and are refused when consent is absent or downloads are off.
- A download ledger is written owner-only.
- Adoption and holds live in memory and end on consent revocation, residency loss or hash loss.
- A transition watchdog cancels only stalled operations.

One finding covers the consent-semantics widening and the threat-model gap. Autopilot is absent from every TB/T entry.

Unverified contracts for the next pass:
- The weight-hash check against the catalog weight_hash (A-004/T-027), in AutopilotStartInventory and publishAutopilotDownload.
- Whether refusal of out-of-set prefetch without consent (handlePrefetchModelRequest) is enforced.
- AutopilotDiskGuard reserve enforcement (T-016).
- Ledger file permissions.
- That re-registration (refreshAutopilotInventoryRegistration) preserves T-053 binding and endpoint-resumption invariants.
- That adoption serving (autopilotServesModel) without a lease does not bypass TB-011 serving authorization.

None of these implementations were supplied.

findings.detail: model-autopilot.md head lines 5-10 and the new sections (~37-130) reverse the base statement (base lines 5-7) that consent does not authorize downloads. A saved opt-in now exposes every verified cached catalog build and permits coordinator-initiated downloads by default. The doc also says neither change bumps the consent `revision`. An operator who consented under the old meaning ('explicitly consented cached models') therefore gains download and set-widening authority without re-consent. The coordinator is trusted, so this is not an adversarial bypass. It does create new provider-side attack surface that no threat-model entry covers: coordinator-driven disk consumption (50 GiB reserve, no default storage cap; related to T-016); fetching and publishing catalog weights (A-004/T-012/T-027 weight-hash verification); and the owner-only `autopilot-downloads.json` ledger. Fix: add a threat-model entry or TB covering Autopilot downloads, set widening, the ledger and placement holds. Also consider requiring a consent revision or explicit re-consent before enabling downloads by default for pre-existing consent records.
findings.title: Existing Autopilot consent now silently authorizes default-on downloads and a wider model set, with no threat-model coverage
